After Muhammad's death in 632 the community needed a political successor, and the caliphate was created to lead it.
Islamic religious authority over the Muslim community gave the caliphate its claim to lead as successor to the Prophet.
Rashidun caliphate armies in the 630s and 640s overthrew the Sasanian Empire, conquering Persia.
Caliphate armies defeated Byzantine forces at Yarmuk and took Syria between roughly 634 and 640.
Caliph Umar's armies invaded Byzantine Egypt in 639 to 641 and took Alexandria, bringing Egypt under the caliphate.
Umayyad caliphate forces crossed into Iberia from 711 and conquered the Visigothic kingdom, creating Al-Andalus.
